h1: Fencing in Garland, TX: Wood Privacy, Repair, Gates and Iron
heroSub: From older Garland streets with 15-year-old wood fences to new east-side lots near Lake Ray Hubbard, get two or three written quotes from independent fence contractors. Call (214) 555-0137.
introHtml:
Fencing in Garland, Texas, mostly comes down to two kinds of yards: older neighborhoods east and northeast of Dallas where a wood fence has stood 15 or 20 years and is leaning, going grey and dropping pickets, and newer east-side subdivisions toward Lake Ray Hubbard where the lot has no fence yet. Either way, the first job is the same: find out what the City of Garland and your HOA allow, then compare written quotes.

White Rock Fence Co is an advertising site. It does not build or repair fences. It connects Garland homeowners with independent fence contractors, so every price below is attributed to the firm that published it and every rule is attributed to the city. Call (214) 555-0137 or email info@whiterockfenceco.com to start.

services.title: Wood privacy fence installation
services.desc: Cedar or pine privacy fences for Garland back yards, including board-on-board. Garland's fence page allows up to eight feet in a residential area, so height is something to settle with the contractor, the City and your HOA.

services.title: Fence repair
services.desc: Leaning sections, rotted posts, missing pickets and storm damage on fences that have stood 15 or 20 years. An independent contractor can tell you in writing whether repair or replacement makes more sense.

services.title: Gate repair and automatic gates
services.desc: Sagging walk gates, dragging drive gates and openers that stopped responding. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask who holds the electrical license.

services.title: Wrought iron fences
services.desc: Ornamental iron or steel for front and side yards. Garland's page limits a front-yard wood or wrought iron fence to 3.5 feet with open spacing, and any front-yard fence needs a permit.

sections.heading: What the City of Garland says about fences
sections.html:
Garland's fence page, which we read as an Internet Archive copy from 2 January 2026 because the city's site was not reachable, lists when a residential fence permit is required: a corner lot (any replacement or new install), a swimming pool in the rear yard, any change to height, location or material, and a new fence where none existed. It lists the permit at $88, made up of $70 plus an $18 processing fee. Confirm the current rules and fee with the City before you sign anything.

The same page says that in a residential area fences may be as tall as eight feet, measured from grade inside the fence around the rear perimeter of the house. In the front yard it allows wood or wrought iron up to 3.5 feet with open spacing and brick or masonry up to 2.5 feet, and it requires a permit for any front-yard fence. A solid privacy fence is a different animal from a front-yard fence, so ask the City exactly where your front yard ends. Next door the rules differ, as the Mesquite, Richardson and Plano pages show.

Corner lots get extra attention. Garland's page says a corner lot with a solid fence needs a visibility clip, which is a cut-back at the corner so drivers can see. Check your plat for easements and ask the City before building on one. Texas has no state fence license, and the page we read does not say whether Garland registers fence contractors, so ask the permit office.

sections.heading: Older fences and newer lots: repair or replace
sections.html:
For a wood fence that has stood 15 or 20 years, the question is repair versus replace. One Dallas contractor's published repair prices run $25 to $60 per board installed, $150 to $400 to pull a single post and set a new footing, and $300 to $800 to straighten a leaning section of 10 to 30 feet (Roof Raiders & Co, Dallas). See the fence repair page for what to ask a contractor.

Once several posts have shifted, or the lean runs the length of a side, repair money starts to look like a down payment on a new fence. Much of the Dallas area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture, so ask any contractor how they will set the posts and get the answer in the quote. After a spring storm, remember that the National Weather Service counts North Texas storms with 58 mph winds as severe. One DFW firm lists storm damage repair at $300 to $1,200 (TX Fence & Deck).

On a new east-side lot with no fence, the job is a new fence, and Garland's page lists a new fence where none existed as a permit trigger. If you are in an HOA, Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023 says an association may not bar a perimeter fence outright but may still regulate the type of fencing. Get the association's approval in writing as well as the City's permit, then look at fence installation for what a full quote should cover.

sections.heading: What fencing costs near Garland and how to compare quotes
sections.html:
The figures below are DFW and Dallas-area numbers, each from the firm that published it, and none is a Garland quote or a price from this site. One DFW firm advertises installed cedar privacy fence at $18 to $28 per linear foot for a standard 6-foot height, while another puts a 6-foot wood privacy fence at $30 to $60. Board-on-board costs more: one firm says about $20 to $36 per linear foot in Dallas, and another says it adds $2 to $5 per foot over a basic dog-ear fence. Ranges vary widely, so use them to spot an outlier, not to set a budget to the dollar.

Garland allows eight feet in a residential area, but we found no Dallas firm's published per-foot price for an 8-foot fence. A national cost guide (Fixr, national figures, not Dallas) puts totals for 150 linear feet at $2,250 to $6,000 for a 6-foot fence and $4,500 to $12,750 for 8 feet. Treat that as a yardstick and expect a contractor to price your 8-foot job on its own. For iron, one Addison firm lists standard residential tubular steel at $30 to $45 per linear foot installed; see the iron fence page.

Ask for two or three written quotes that name the same board type, height, post material, gate count, who handles the permit and who calls 811. Texas811 says that when you hire a contractor, calling 811 two business days before digging is the contractor's responsibility. Compare them line by line using the Dallas fence cost guide, and for drive gates see gate repair. Call (214) 555-0137 to get started.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to replace a fence in Garland?
faq.a: Garland's fence page lists a permit for corner lots (any replacement or install), a rear-yard pool, changing height, location or material, a new fence where none existed, and any front-yard fence. It lists the fee at $88 ($70 plus an $18 processing fee) in the copy we read from January 2026. That list does not mention a same-height, same-place, same-material swap on a non-corner lot, so ask the City before you assume you are exempt.

faq.q: How tall can a fence be in Garland?
faq.a: Garland's page says residential fences may be as tall as eight feet, measured from grade inside the fence around the rear perimeter of the house. In the front yard it allows wood or wrought iron up to 3.5 feet with open spacing, and brick or masonry up to 2.5 feet. Check your lot's measurements with the City and your HOA before ordering materials.

faq.q: Who pays for a fence shared with my Garland neighbor?
faq.a: We found no Texas statute on splitting boundary-fence costs. Texas Law Help, a legal-aid site, says that if both neighbors use a fence straddling the line, both own it and would share the cost of repairing and replacing it, while a fence wholly on one lot belongs to that owner. This is general information, not legal advice, and an HOA may also control the type of fencing under Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023.

faq.q: What does it cost to fix an automatic gate in Garland?
faq.a: One DFW gate company's page about Garland sliding-gate repair says the average automatic gate repair is about $900 and many jobs fall between $550 and $1,500, citing Angi; we could not confirm the Angi figure. Another DFW firm says problems caught early cost $100 to $300 to fix, with motor replacements at $1,000 or more. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical license.
